title: The First Hour
subtitle: Prime, prayed at sunrise, roughly 6 a.m.
intro: The First Hour sanctifies the dawn. Read it after the Morning Rule when the schedule allows, or alone, standing toward the icons. The Hours are short, about five minutes each.
source: Common Orthodox Horologion (Jordanville and Hapgood traditions). Full Psalm and Troparion text will land in the next content drop; the structural shell here is correct.

prayers.title: Opening blessing
prayers.instruction: Bless the beginning of the Hour:
prayers.text: Through the prayers of our holy fathers, O Lord Jesus Christ our God, have mercy on us. Amen.

prayers.title: Trisagion through the Lord's Prayer
prayers.instruction: Pray the usual beginning. Cite the standard text from the Morning Rule if you have it open.
prayers.text: (see Morning Rule: Heavenly King · Trisagion · Most Holy Trinity · Lord have mercy · Glory · Now and ever · Our Father.)

prayers.title: The three Psalms of the First Hour
prayers.instruction: Psalms 5, 89, and 100. Read in full when time allows; the citation links open the Septuagint numbering on this site.
prayers.text: Psalm 5 (Hear my words, O Lord) · Psalm 89 (Lord, Thou hast been our refuge) · Psalm 100 (Mercy and judgment will I sing unto Thee, O Lord).

prayers.title: Troparion of the day
prayers.instruction: Insert the troparion appointed for today; the simple form below applies to ordinary weekdays of Great Lent and the fasts.
prayers.text: In the morning hear my voice, O my King and my God.

prayers.title: Dismissal of the Hour
prayers.text: O Christ the true Light, who enlightenest and sanctifiest every man that cometh into the world: let the light of Thy countenance be signed upon us, that in it we may behold the unapproachable Light, and direct our steps in the doing of Thy commandments, through the prayers of Thy most pure Mother and of all the saints. Amen.
